candidate_claim_transitions.statement_of_discharge: codes/loop/loop.sbatch:287 adds KTG_PARTITIONS="${KTG_PARTITIONS:-b300 b200}" and :288-303 rewrites pick_partition() to iterate that list, remember the candidate it is testing in `last`, and fall back to `echo "${last:-b200}"` instead of a literal b200. Four code lines changed in all (the `local` line, the `for` line, the `last=` line and the fallback), plus the KTG_PARTITIONS assignment, the contract comment at :20-24 and the section comment at :258-286. Semantics, documented in the file: candidates are separated by WHITESPACE and tried in order; a candidate may itself be a comma-joined Slurm partition SET such as b200,l40s, because Slurm accepts --partition=b200,l40s and starts the job in whichever of those partitions can run it first, and the free-GPU count for such a candidate is the sum over its members since sinfo -p takes the same comma list; comma is therefore Slurm's own spelling and never a candidate separator, so a purely comma-separated value is one multi-partition candidate. "b300 b200,l40s" is exactly the decided behaviour. resubmit() is unchanged and already passes the resolved string to both the compute-budget pre-flight (:548) and sbatch (:554); the compute-budget script's accepted set already contains b200,l40s / l40s,b200 / b300,b200 / b300,b200,l40s, and loop.sbatch itself has no partition-consistency pre-flight to teach about comma lists (grep for SLURM_JOB_PARTITION in loop.sbatch: exit 1). Propagation is the same path as KTG_MAX_CHAIN, KTG_MAX_FAILS and KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS -- a plain ${VAR:-default} assignment, which keeps the export attribute of a value that arrived from the environment, plus an sbatch call with no --export on any non-comment line (grep count 0; the 3 textual matches are all in comments), so Slurm's default --export=ALL carries it down the chain. Closing conditions, all verbatim in evidence/loop_resume/repair_partitions.txt: (1) PART 2, pick_partition extracted with awk from BOTH files and run against a node fixture: with the knob unset, before and after agree on every one of 27 cells of the b300 state matrix (IDLE, MIXED, ALLOCATED, RESERVED, DRAIN, DOWN, MAINT, IDLE+RESERVED, MIXED+DRAIN x alloc 0/7/8), including the all-busy fallback. (2) PART 2 S1-S4 and PART 3 L1-L5: with KTG_PARTITIONS='b300 b200,l40s', b300 free gives --partition=b300 before and after; b300 RESERVED gives b200 before and b200,l40s after; b300 RESERVED + b200 full gives b200 before and b200,l40s after; nothing free anywhere gives b200 before and b200,l40s after (the last-candidate fallback). (3) PART 2 S6/S7: 11 knob spellings, including tab, multiple-space, newline, leading and trailing whitespace, a pure comma list, a single partition and the empty string (which takes the default list); and a multi-partition candidate is eligible when EITHER member has a free GPU. (4) PART 3 L7: the successor. resubmit()'s sbatch call carries no --export; the sbatch shim records KTG_PARTITIONS='b300 b200,l40s' in its own environment, which is what --export=ALL copies into the successor's job; links 2 and 3, run with exactly that value, each resolve --partition=b200,l40s and hand the same value on. (5) PART 3 L6: an unallowed candidate is caught by the only gate in the resubmit path -- the compute-budget check prints VIOLATION, resubmit() says 'refusing to chain' and NO sbatch is issued. PART 3 L9: check.sh on the live cluster exits 0 for b300, b200, l40s, b200,l40s and b300,b200,l40s. (6) PART 4: unchanged behaviour. The wave-3 validator's own v2_regress.sh, v3_seeds.sh and w3v_common.sh, extracted verbatim from evidence/wave3_prelaunch_repairs/validation_harness.txt and run UNMODIFIED: the 46-link regression set A-J, K1-K6, L1/L2, M, N, O, P3-P5 and the 51-link seed matrix T1-T5. candidate_result_row.claim: codes/loop/synchronous_loop_9x9.sh and codes/loop/export_model_for_selfplay_9x9.sh carry 'set -eu -o pipefail' in the body, so errexit, nounset and pipefail hold whether the file is executed or handed to `bash` -- the form loop.sbatch uses -- and a failure anywhere in the archive-staging section stops the loop instead of being followed by cycle 1 out of an incomplete archive. In codes/loop/loop.sbatch the .failcount accounting, the minimum-runtime penalty, the breaker and the scancel of the queued afterany successor live in one function, finalize(), run from an EXIT trap installed immediately after resubmit(), and finalize sorts the ways a link can end into five classes. A deliberate storage stop -- the loop exiting 3 WITH $BASEDIR/STOP present, the file the loop writes before that exit -- cancels the successor and spends no attempt. A scheduler termination -- SIGTERM to this wrapper, recorded by a TERM trap installed before the resubmit, or a 128+15 loop status on a link that has run at least KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS -- keeps the queued successor, which is the resume itself, and leaves .failcount alone unless the link completed cycles, in which case the run of consecutive failures is cleared. A SIGTERM seen during the pre-flight ends the link before the loop is launched. A loop failure already recorded when a later SIGTERM arrives is counted as the failure it is. A pre-flight failure counts, with the fast-failure penalty, and cancels the successor. A loop failure counts and cancels only when the breaker trips; an exit 3 without STOP is one of these. A cycle that ran and exited 0 resets the count, an exit 0 that never ran the loop leaves it, and a link that advanced $BASEDIR/.cycles_completed restarts the failure run, so KTG_MAX_FAILS means three failures with no completed cycle between them. Neither loop.sbatch nor synchronous_loop_9x9.sh contains a storage threshold or its own du/df/quotas.py measurement: both call codes/data_budget/scratch_guard.sh and honour its exit code, with no --root passed. The three upstream defect repairs (o09, o13 config half, o17) admitted in the earlier rows are unchanged, and a KTG_STAGE_ONLY dry run from the real scratch clone stages the same 80 files byte-for-byte before and after this repair. NOT covered: a SIGKILL end -- KillWait expiry, cgroup OOM, node failure -- runs no handler, writes nothing and simply lets the queued successor resume, shown by scenario M; a loop status 143 after the runtime floor is still read as a scheduler termination whatever caused it; a SIGTERM already seen outranks a deterministic pre-flight failure that follows it, self-correcting in one extra link; and a link that completes a cycle before failing never accumulates toward the breaker. Every chain-state integer under $BASEDIR -- .failcount, .chain_depth and .cycles_completed -- is now read through one function, read_counter() in loop.sbatch, which trims whitespace, requires a plain decimal of at most 18 digits and parses it with 10#, so a leading-zero value such as 08 or 09 is read as 8 or 9 rather than aborting the enclosing command list as an invalid octal literal, an unparsable value reads as 0 instead of aborting, and a value past 2^63 cannot wrap; an unparsable .failcount or .chain_depth additionally prints a WARNING line naming the file and the value that was read. finalize() therefore writes the count, writes .breaker_tripped and cancels the queued successor for every seed, and the wrapper reaches its resubmit for every seed. VALIDATOR QUALIFICATION (o36): that holds for every VALUE a state file can hold, and a corrupt .failcount costs at most one extra link because finalize() overwrites it with a plain decimal on the next failure (harness X8: abc, then 2, then 4 and the breaker on link 2; X8b at the slow-failure floor trips on link 3; X9: the corrupt value persists only across scheduler-terminated links, with a WARNING each). It does NOT hold when the file cannot be WRITTEN: no write of .failcount or .chain_depth is checked, so a .failcount that is a directory, unreadable or read-only is read as 0 (no WARNING when cat fails) and never advances -- every link prints 'chain continues' and queues its successor, a crash loop bounded only by KTG_MAX_CHAIN (X3, X4, X5); the same fail-open direction applies to the operator knobs, which are not read through read_counter: KTG_MAX_FAILS=abc makes every '-ge' test false so the breaker never trips (X10b: 2, 4, 6 with a successor each link) and KTG_MAX_CHAIN=abc removes the depth bound (X10c); KTG_MAX_FAILS=08 aborts finalize() at :375 after the count is written (X10a, the worker's residual). The loop's own CHANGE 10 writer carries the same trim / guard / width / 10# parse, so a seeded 08 self-heals to 9 on the next completed cycle instead of killing the loop after every cycle. No writer in codes/ can produce a padded value in the first place (no printf %0Nd, no seq -w; every write is an unpadded $(( )) result), so the exposure only ever needed a hand-edited or foreign-written file. Nothing here ran on a GPU or under a real scheduler. AMENDMENT (wave 3, R1/R6/R5). loop.sbatch:8 declares --cpus-per-task=32; the wrapper types no CPU count at all -- REQ_CPUS is KTG_CPUS_PER_TASK read from codes/loop/knobs_9x9.env, whose sha256 is logged at pre-flight; a knob file that is unreadable, or that carries KTG_MAX_FAILS/KTG_MAX_CHAIN/KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS, is not sourced at all, resubmit() then refuses to chain and the pre-flight exits 2; a granted SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK != KTG_CPUS_PER_TASK, or either engine cfg declaring a numGameThreads != KTG_NUM_GAME_THREADS, is a pre-flight failure (exit 2) that cancels the queued successor. The policy script named by mission.json compute.policyCheck passes at --gpus 1 --cpus 32 --partition b200. loop.sbatch starts codes/eval/stage_monitor.sh over $BASEDIR/monitor with its own pid as the sampling root after env.sh and the knob asserts (a missing sampler is a pre-flight failure), and stops it as the first statement of finalize() after FINALIZED=1, || true; synchronous_loop_9x9.sh retags the samples cycleN at the top of each cycle when $BASEDIR/monitor/monitor.run exists. The link samples at KTG_MON_PS_INTERVAL=1 / KTG_MON_GPU_INTERVAL=5; stage_monitor.sh's own defaults stay the smoke's 0.2 s / 2 s. synchronous_loop_9x9.sh runs codes/eval/check_pos_len_npz.py at loop start and again between selfplay and shuffle in every cycle, over the npz under $BASEDIR/selfplay newer than $BASEDIR/.pos_len_checked (all of them when the marker is absent), skipping cleanly at 0 files and touching the marker after a pass; a mismatch names the file and ends the cycle with exit 1 BEFORE the shuffle, instead of the train-time assert at data_processing_pytorch.py:91 a whole selfplay stage later. VALIDATOR QUALIFICATIONS (2026-09-04, record results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/evidence/wave3_prelaunch_repairs/validation.md). (i) The stray-knob guard is a line-anchored grep for NAME= at the start of a line: a knob file carrying a plain KTG_MAX_FAILS= / KTG_MAX_CHAIN= / KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS= assignment is refused before sourcing (V1f, V1i), but the spelling export KTG_MAX_FAILS=1 is sourced and retunes the breaker for that link (V1g: failcount 0/1, breaker on the first failure), and a $NAME reference to an unset variable anywhere in the knob file aborts the wrapper at :186 under set -u BEFORE the resubmit and BEFORE the EXIT trap, so that link ends with no successor and no accounting (V1j, the o26 class); both need an edit of the knob file, whose every non-comment line at HEAD is NAME=digits with no $ (o42). (ii) stage_monitor.sh stop kills the pids listed in monitor.pids without checking what they are: after a SIGKILLed link (no finalize, monitor.run and monitor.pids left behind, V6e) a successor that fails its pre-flight BEFORE its own start runs stop from finalize on the stale pids and kills whatever same-user process now holds them (V6g: an unrelated sleep of this user was killed); a successor that reaches start overwrites both files first. Needs SIGKILL plus a deterministic pre-flight failure plus pid reuse by a same-user process; bounded to one kill; recorded as o42 (b). (iii) The pos_len guard is an mtime test: a file whose mtime predates the marker (rsync -a / cp -p onto a resumed tree, V5e) or a marker whose mtime is in the future (clock skew, V5f) is skipped until the marker is removed, and a file written between the pre-shuffle check and the shuffle (V5k) is shuffled unguarded that cycle and refused at the next link's loop-start check; the guard costs 0.53 s for 400 npz (V5g). (iv) The sampler survives no end of a link: a process-group SIGTERM (walltime form, V6c) ends it, a wrapper-only SIGTERM leaves it to finalize's stop (V6d, 35 samples, 0 alive after), a SIGKILL leaves the run file behind but the samplers end on kill -0 of the dead root within one interval (V6e, 0 alive after 3 s); its cost is about 6 % of one core at 1 s on a 1751-process login node (90 ms per ps sweep, V6j). (v) The dry run stages 87 files / 28880227 B, not the 80 / 28702024 B the task file cites: the scratch clone's python/katago and python/muon now carry 13 __pycache__ files that upstream's cp -r copies into every dated archive; before and after are byte-identical (manifest diff exit 0). (vi) The compare of SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK is skipped when the variable is unset (V1c); that is not a hole in a real link because the batch environment of every job so far carried it (cfg9x9 job 298359 printed SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK = 24, both smoke jobs printed cpus_per_task = 24 from it) and job 299366 shows CPUs/Task=32. AMENDMENT (fifth repair, o44). pick_partition() no longer carries a hard-coded partition list: codes/loop/loop.sbatch:287 reads KTG_PARTITIONS, defaulting to the historical "b300 b200", and :288-303 tries those candidates in order and falls back to the LAST one rather than a literal b200. A candidate may be a comma-joined Slurm partition set ("b200,l40s"), whose free-GPU count is summed over its members because sinfo -p takes the same comma list; comma is Slurm's spelling and never a candidate separator. The decided behaviour, documented in the file, is "b300 when it has a free GPU and no reservation or drain blocks it, otherwise the multi-partition set". resubmit() passes that resolved string unchanged to both the compute-budget pre-flight and sbatch, and KTG_PARTITIONS reaches every successor on the same path as KTG_MAX_CHAIN / KTG_MAX_FAILS / KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS -- a plain ${VAR:-default} assignment plus an sbatch call with no --export of its own, so Slurm's default --export=ALL applies. That closes the asymmetry the production_chain_9x9 launcher held at its pre-submission gate: a first link submitted --partition=b200,l40s used to queue links 2..9 on b300/b200 only. With the knob unset the function is byte-identical in behaviour to the pre-repair one over the whole b300 state matrix. NOT covered: the list is expanded unquoted, so a shell metacharacter in the knob globs against the job's cwd, and an unallowed candidate of any spelling is caught only by the compute-budget pre-flight, which refuses to chain rather than submitting; loop.sbatch still has no partition-consistency pre-flight of its own. Whether an L40S node can run the engine at all is a separate open question (the binary carries no sm_89 image) owned by another packet, so this amendment makes the multi-partition set REACHABLE, not proven runnable.
